messages:
maria: quick heads-up, canary post-kernel-routing change is showing a tail latency spike on small convo models. looks allocator-related, possibly LRU buffer pool churn + tiny splits. repro on 2xA100 test nodes.
cheng: can you paste the profiler snip? what knobs were set for the canary?
maria: running with default alloc knobs we usually use for canary: `expandable_segments: true`, `max_split_size_mb: 64`, `garbage_collection_threshold: 0.12`. KV cache warmup trace shows lots of ~8-32KB allocations during prompt prep.
profiling-bot: quick profile summary (canary-2a100):
```
heap_frag_ratio: 0.34
alloc_calls_per_s: 18.2k
avg_alloc_size: 10.6KB
avg_free_latency_ms: 0.9
num_small_splits: 42% of splits
LRU_evictions_s: 1.7k/min (bursting)
```
cheng: that eviction rate looks high. when splits are small we fragment slabs and force extra coalesces. might be exacerbated by batching heuristics sending many short sequences.
eva: did kernel routing change increase small-buffer allocations? I remember a change that favored a narrow attention kernel for short sequences, creating more intermediate buffers.
maria: yes, kernel routing now picks small-seq GEMM kernel for <64 tokens which allocates a temp buffer per batch-item. combined with auto-batching spikes, we get simultaneous frees -> fragmentation oscillation.
sam: two quick experiments: (1) bump `max_split_size_mb` to 128 to reduce small-split prevalence, (2) temporarily set `expandable_segments=false` to force coalesced slabs, see if eviction drops. canary run queued.
ops-bot: canary job started: `canary-run 3460011223 --knobs max_split_size_mb=128 expandable_segments=false`
profiling-bot: early tail numbers after 10 minutes: avg latency +9%, p95 +22%, p99 +38% (compared to baseline). fragmentation metric down to 0.18, LRU_evictions 420/min. small-splits dropped to 18%.
cheng: interesting—fragmentation improved but tail latency still worse. suggests GC behavior or buffer reuse penalty. what was `garbage_collection_threshold`?
maria: left at 0.12 for baseline. sam suggested raising to 0.25 to trigger earlier GC sweep when fragmentation starts.
eva: before doing that, try enabling an LRU pad so the pool doesn't evict on borderline hits — small change: `pool_lru_pad_pct=10`. that keeps some slack to avoid immediate reuse thrash.
sam: running three-parallel canaries: A) max_split=128 + expandable=false, B) same + pool_lru_pad=10, C) same + gc_threshold=0.25. will post results in ~20m.
profiling-bot: canary results (short):
A) tail higher, fragmentation down, eviction down.
B) tail improved vs A: p95 -8%, p99 -12% and lower alloc churn.
C) tail worse than B: GC pauses introduced slight tail bumps, p99 spiky.
maria: conclusion so far: reducing tiny splits helps fragmentation, but aggressive GC creates pause spikes. LRU pad gives best tail improvement without GC-induced pauses.
cheng: for longer term: (1) consider moving temporary kernel buffers into a reusable transient pool keyed by kernel type+size, (2) adjust batching heuristic to cap per-request short-seq concurrency, (3) expose pool_lru_pad and per-kernel transient pool sizing as runtime knobs.
eva: add an integration test that simulates KV-warmup pattern (many small allocations) to detect this regression in CI.
sam: filed infra ticket: INFRA-1987 to add CI scenario + a canary that varies `max_split_size_mb`.
maria: opened follow-up: PERF-452: add transient-kernel-pool prototype + telemetry for per-kernel temp allocation counts. will pair with eng-runtime next week.
cheng: thanks. small note for docs — document interplay: `expandable_segments` + small-split prevalence + kernel temp buffers -> fragmentation path. saved me a day. :thumbsup:
